note: One entry per subject. Set "offered": false to leave a subject out of the batch. Every subject produces five flyers: spotlight, tutoring, fact, tip and quiz.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.tagline: Say it clearly. Write it well.
subjects.summary: English Language builds the reading, writing and speaking skills that every other subject depends on.
subjects.fact: The verb “run” has more than 600 separate meanings in the Oxford English Dictionary.

tip.title: Plan before you write
tip.text: Spend five minutes on a plan: three main points and an ending. A planned composition reads better and saves time.

quiz.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
quiz.explain: It’s means “it is”; your means “belonging to you”.

subjects.name: Literature in English
subjects.summary: Literature in English trains students to read poetry, drama and novels closely, and to write strong essays backed by evidence.
subjects.fact: Shakespeare is credited with the first recorded use of hundreds of English words, including “bedroom” and “eyeball”.

tip.title: Point, evidence, explain
tip.text: Make a point, quote a short piece of evidence, then explain how the writer’s words create the effect.

quiz.q: A comparison that uses “like” or “as” is called a…
quiz.explain: “As brave as a lion” is a simile.

tutoring.headline: Essays that prove you read closely.

subjects.name: ChiShona
subjects.summary: ChiShona builds fluent reading, writing and speaking in our language, along with the literature, culture and wisdom it carries.
subjects.fact: Clement Doke’s 1931 report on unifying the Shona dialects laid the foundation for the standard written ChiShona used in schools today.

tip.title: Learn tsumo with their meanings
tip.text: Proverbs earn marks in composition and comprehension. Learn five tsumo a week, each with its meaning and an example of when to use it.

quiz.q: Which ChiShona word means “school”?
quiz.explain: Mvura is water, imba is house and sadza is the staple maize meal.

tutoring.headline: Strong ChiShona, from grammar to tsumo.

subjects.name: isiNdebele
subjects.summary: isiNdebele develops confident reading, writing and speaking, and opens up the literature, history and culture of the language.
subjects.fact: isiNdebele has click sounds, written with the letters c, q and x, which it shares with isiZulu and isiXhosa.

tip.title: Read aloud every day
tip.text: Reading isiNdebele aloud for ten minutes a day builds vocabulary, spelling and the rhythm you need for poetry.

quiz.q: Which isiNdebele word means “school”?
quiz.explain: Amanzi is water, indlu is house and isitshwala is the staple maize meal.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.summary: Mathematics builds the problem-solving that every science and technical subject relies on, from algebra to statistics.
subjects.fact: The Indian mathematician Brahmagupta wrote rules for calculating with zero in the year 628.

tip.title: Show every step
tip.text: Method marks reward working even when the final answer is wrong. Write each step on its own line.

quiz.q: Solve: 3x + 5 = 20
quiz.explain: Subtract 5 to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3: x = 5.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.tagline: For students who want more maths.
subjects.summary: Additional Mathematics stretches strong mathematicians with calculus, logarithms and vectors, which is ideal preparation for A Level sciences and engineering.
subjects.fact: Isaac Newton and Gottfried Leibniz developed calculus independently in the late 1600s, then argued for years over who came first.

tip.title: Learn the standard results
tip.text: Memorise the standard derivatives and integrals, such as those of sin x, cos x and eˣ. They come up in nearly every paper.

quiz.q: What is the derivative of x³?
quiz.explain: Bring the power down and reduce it by one: 3x².

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.summary: Computer Science teaches programming, how computers and networks work, and how to solve problems with algorithms.
subjects.fact: The first computer “bug” written into a logbook was a real moth, found inside the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947.

tip.title: Trace your code by hand
tip.text: Use a trace table to follow each variable line by line. It finds logic errors faster than guessing.

quiz.q: What is the binary number 1010 in denary?

subjects.name: Combined Science
subjects.summary: Combined Science covers biology, chemistry and physics together, with practical work that builds real laboratory skills.
topics: Cells, nutrition and the human body
Matter, reactions and the periodic table
subjects.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.

tip.title: Learn your units
tip.text: Many marks are lost on units. Learn them with each formula: force in newtons, energy in joules, current in amperes.

quiz.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
quiz.explain: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

tutoring.headline: One subject, three sciences, all covered.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.summary: Biology explores life from cells to ecosystems, including the human body, plants, genetics and the environment.
subjects.fact: An adult human body is made of roughly 30 trillion cells, with about as many bacteria living alongside them.

tip.title: Draw it, label it
tip.text: Practise labelled diagrams of the heart, the leaf and the cell. Clear labels earn marks that long answers miss.

quiz.q: Which part of the cell contains the genetic material?
quiz.explain: The cell’s DNA is stored in the nucleus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.summary: Chemistry explains what substances are made of and how they react, from the periodic table to organic molecules such as the aldehydes.
topics: Atomic structure and the periodic table
subjects.fact: A teaspoon of water (5 g) holds about 1.7 × 10²³ water molecules. That is 5 ÷ 18 moles, times Avogadro’s number.

tip.title: Balance every equation
tip.text: Count each type of atom on both sides. Change the numbers in front of formulae, never the formulae themselves.

quiz.q: Which functional group do all aldehydes contain?
quiz.explain: Aldehydes end in –CHO, like ethanal, CH₃CHO.

tutoring.headline: Chemistry, one reaction at a time.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.summary: Physics explains motion, energy, electricity, waves and the atom, and teaches students to model the world with mathematics.
subjects.fact: Sound travels about four times faster through water than through air: roughly 1,480 m/s compared with 343 m/s.

tip.title: Write the formula first
tip.text: Write the formula, substitute the values with their units, then calculate. Examiners award marks for each step.

quiz.q: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
quiz.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

tutoring.headline: Physics problems, solved step by step.

subjects.name: Agriculture
subjects.summary: Agriculture combines biology, chemistry and business to grow crops and raise animals well, with plenty of hands-on practical work.
subjects.fact: Maize was domesticated in Mexico about 9,000 years ago from a wild grass called teosinte.

tip.title: Know your NPK
tip.text: N, P and K are nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Learn what each does for a crop and the signs when it is missing.

quiz.q: Which nutrient mainly promotes leafy growth in crops?
quiz.explain: Nitrogen drives leaf and stem growth; without it, leaves turn yellow.

tutoring.headline: Agriculture in theory and in the field.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.summary: Geography studies landscapes, weather, population and resources, and how people and the environment shape each other.
subjects.fact: Victoria Falls, Mosi-oa-Tunya, is about 1.7 km wide and 108 m high, one of the largest sheets of falling water on Earth.

tip.title: Practise map reading
tip.text: Map-work questions are reliable marks. Practise grid references, scale and bearings until they are automatic.

quiz.q: On a 1:50 000 map, a six-figure grid reference locates a point to the nearest…
quiz.explain: Each extra pair of figures divides a 1 km grid square into tenths: 100 m.

tutoring.headline: Geography, from map work to case studies.

subjects.name: History
subjects.summary: History studies the people and events that shaped Zimbabwe, Africa and the world, and teaches students to weigh evidence.
subjects.fact: The walls of the Great Enclosure at Great Zimbabwe were built without mortar and stand up to 11 metres high.

tip.title: Use dates and evidence
tip.text: Strong history answers name specific dates, people and places. Build a timeline for every topic.

quiz.q: Great Zimbabwe lies near which modern city?
quiz.explain: Great Zimbabwe is about 30 km from Masvingo, close to home for Royal Crest.

subjects.name: Heritage Studies
subjects.tagline: Who we are and where we stand.
subjects.summary: Heritage Studies explores Zimbabwe’s culture, values and national identity, and the rights and duties of every citizen.
topics: Zimbabwe in Africa and the world
subjects.fact: Zimbabwe has five UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Great Zimbabwe, Khami Ruins, Mana Pools, Matobo Hills and Victoria Falls.

tip.title: Link facts to examples
tip.text: Back every point with a Zimbabwean example: a heritage site, a festival or a section of the Constitution.

quiz.q: Which of these is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Zimbabwe?
quiz.explain: UNESCO listed the Matobo Hills in 2003.

subjects.name: Family & Religious Studies
subjects.summary: Family and Religious Studies looks at African Traditional Religion, Christianity, Islam and other faiths, and the values that guide families and communities.
subjects.fact: Parts of the Bible have been translated into more than 3,000 languages, including ChiShona and isiNdebele.

tip.title: Compare the faiths
tip.text: Many questions ask how religions agree or differ. Prepare short comparison tables for key beliefs and practices.

quiz.q: In African Traditional Religion, the departed family members who guide the living are known as…
quiz.explain: Ancestral spirits, vadzimu in ChiShona and amadlozi in isiNdebele, guide and protect the family.

tutoring.headline: Clear answers on faith and values.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.summary: Accounting teaches how to record, organise and report financial information, skills every business and household needs.
subjects.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping was first set out in print in 1494 by Luca Pacioli, a friend of Leonardo da Vinci.

tip.title: Debit left, credit right
tip.text: Keep T-accounts neat: debits on the left, credits on the right, and total both sides every time.

quiz.q: In double entry, every transaction is recorded…
quiz.explain: Every transaction has a debit entry and an equal credit entry.

subjects.name: Commerce
subjects.summary: Commerce explains trade, banking, insurance, transport and communication: everything that moves goods from producers to consumers.
subjects.fact: The world’s first banknotes were used in China about 1,000 years ago, during the Song dynasty.

tip.title: Use real examples
tip.text: Back up answers with examples from Zimbabwean businesses and markets you know.

quiz.q: Insurance mainly helps a business to…
quiz.explain: Many pay small premiums so that the few who suffer a loss can be compensated.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.summary: Economics studies how people, businesses and governments make choices with limited resources, from prices to inflation.
subjects.fact: Adam Smith’s “The Wealth of Nations”, published in 1776, is often called the first modern book of economics.

tip.title: Draw the diagram
tip.text: Supply and demand diagrams earn marks on their own. Label the axes, the curves and the equilibrium every time.

quiz.q: If demand rises and supply stays the same, the price will usually…
quiz.explain: More buyers competing for the same goods pushes the price up.

subjects.name: Technical Graphics
subjects.tagline: Draw it right, build it right.
subjects.summary: Technical Graphics teaches precise drawing: geometry, orthographic and isometric projection, and the drawings engineers and builders work from.
subjects.fact: In first-angle projection, used across Europe and Africa, the plan is drawn below the front view. In third-angle projection, used in the USA, it sits above.

tip.title: Choose the right pencil
tip.text: Use a 2H pencil for construction lines and an HB for outlines. Clean, consistent lines earn presentation marks.

quiz.q: How many views are usually drawn in orthographic projection?
quiz.explain: The front view, the end view and the plan.

subjects.name: Building Technology
subjects.summary: Building Technology covers how buildings are designed and built, with practical skills in materials, bricklaying and construction.
subjects.fact: Concrete reaches most of its strength in its first 28 days, but keeps getting slowly stronger for years as the cement reacts with water.

tip.title: Know the bonds
tip.text: Learn the common brick bonds, stretcher, English and Flemish, and sketch each one from memory.

quiz.q: Concrete is made by mixing cement, water and…
quiz.explain: Sand is the fine aggregate and crushed stone the coarse aggregate.

subjects.name: Wood Technology
subjects.tagline: Made by hand, made to last.
subjects.summary: Wood Technology and Design teaches students to plan, design and make quality projects in timber, using hand tools and machines safely.
subjects.fact: You can tell a tree’s age from its growth rings: in a climate with seasons, each ring is one year of growth.

tip.title: Mark out twice, cut once
tip.text: Accurate marking out is half of a good joint. Check every measurement before you cut.

quiz.q: Which joint is known for its interlocking, fan-shaped tails and pins?
quiz.explain: Dovetails lock together and resist being pulled apart.

tutoring.headline: Skills for projects you are proud of.

subjects.name: Metal Technology
subjects.summary: Metal Technology and Design covers metals, measuring, marking out, cutting, joining and finishing, with practical projects in the workshop.
subjects.fact: Steel is mostly iron with a little carbon, usually under 2%. Add chromium and you get stainless steel.

tip.title: Measure with care
tip.text: Learn to read a vernier caliper and a micrometer to their smallest division before you start any project.

quiz.q: Which of these is an alloy?
quiz.explain: Brass is a mixture of copper and zinc.

subjects.name: Food Technology
subjects.summary: Food Technology and Design covers nutrition, food science and safe food handling, and designing and making dishes.
subjects.fact: Honey can keep for thousands of years: archaeologists have found honey that was still edible in ancient Egyptian tombs.

tip.title: Name the nutrient
tip.text: When a question asks why a food is good for you, name the nutrient and say what it does in the body.

quiz.q: Which nutrient is the body’s main source of energy?
quiz.explain: Carbohydrates, as in sadza and bread, provide most of our energy.
